title: Monotonic timestamps may lack sufficient resolution
environment: Observed runtime and injected-clock controls. This is not a universal defect in every monotonic-clock implementation or Python version.
goal: Enforce a strictly increasing receive watermark for a high-rate stream.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Monotonicity was assumed to imply enough resolution to distinguish each arrival.
what_worked: Historical correction: Use one high-resolution monotonic clock consistently for receive times, age, deadlines and latency; preserve source-order checks. Verification reported by the source: A regression quantized time to 1/64 second at 120 callbacks/second: the old path aborted, the precise path accepted 120. Threaded rate/burst/stall tests and a later 1,200-callback live run passed.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: Separate callbacks received equal coarse timestamps and were rejected as out of order.
why: Confirmed: clock quantization was too coarse for callback cadence; this was independent of the unresolved native hang.
improved_method: Test clock resolution against burst arrival rates. Distinguish source time, receive time and consumer cadence; do not fabricate epsilon timestamps to conceal collisions.
when_to_use: Observed runtime and injected-clock controls. This is not a universal defect in every monotonic-clock implementation or Python version.
when_not_to_use: This is not a universal defect in every monotonic-clock implementation or Python version.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
